Kias making self-driving cars more human: I went for a ride

The problem still persists. The AI is reactive. It is not pro-active.

As a human when I drive my car

  • I look through windshields to see what the car does before the car in front of me.
  • I watch the person in my back mirror, check if they are texting, or playing with some other device.
  • I can see if the person in front of me is an old person (tends to wear a hat in the car).
  • I look at changing light at the road at night to detect a car coming from a corner that I cannot see.
  • I look at window reflections and road mirrors that gives clues if there is a bicycle or car in my blind spot.
  • I watch other people like kids to determine if there may be other kids playing around that I have not seen.
  • I watch the dog owner to see if that dog he is walking with is about to run over the street or not.

There is no way that these autonomous cars can be that pro-active.

You are far too good a driver to be their target market. They are after the texting and eating while knee steering individual that also has the music too loud to hear anything going on. I for one would feel safer is those nuters were off the road and these cars were in their place. At least you know it is always paying full attention and has a near perfect reaction time.

It is only because I see these self driving cars stories that I started to question myself what I am doing subconsciously.

At first I thought these self driving cars were great, but then reality hits me that these cars only self-drive at places where I don't need them to drive me. And these places I drive subconsciously, basically daydreaming, not even recording where I have been or what I have seen.

I only start to realize what I am doing (that list) because I got curious if a self driving car would do it better. And so far I see no point in paying such a big price for something that does not work when I need it.

The traffic I have to go through daily, would mean that such a self driving car would just stop and wait until the traffic jam is over. It wouldn't move because all other none-self driving cars would jump in front of it because they know that it is going to stop anyway.

Oh no doubt a traffic jam or a busy T intersection would throw them for a loop. I guess for those scenarios basically every car would have to be autonomous and communicating with each other. Either way, we are a long ways off from self driving cars in busy downtown cities, poor weather conditions and heavy traffic.

Even for long road trips, where I would love to have one, I couldn't justify the cost though, since I'm poor.
